libx.intro: A library check reads your music folders and the songs' tags. Everything below adds more, and each is off until you switch it on: some take a lot of this computer's time, some ask services online.
libx.sound_analysis_note: Listens to every song once, on this computer, for "more like this", similar artists, radio by sound, smart play, and even volume for songs without ReplayGain tags. It's the heaviest job here: on a modest computer about a song a second, using up to half the processor, so a big library takes hours the first time.
libx.heavy_note: For sound analysis and AI listening. They pause between songs, so music never waits for them.
libx.when_idle: Only while no music is playing
libx.artist_info_note: Sends artist names to Deezer, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, after each library check that finds new artists. Pictures in your own folders always win.

libx.more_pictures_note: (from the sources you choose below, with credits. Commons and fanart.tv use MusicBrainz to find the right artist. Each artist's pictures are fetched the first time they're shown.)
libx.picture_limits_note: These apply to extra artist pictures. Downloaded images are resized before they enter the cache. The cache limit also covers album art and thumbnails; existing files stay when you lower it.

libx.sources_note: Choose automatic sources here. MusicBrainz identifies artists and albums when enabled above. Source changes are applied as each artist is checked again.

libx.allow_remote: Allow remote image display (visitors load images from the provider)
libx.src_unsplash: Unsplash (browse and select, remote display only)
libx.browse_note: Open these libraries to find artist photos. For licensed images, use Manage pictures on an artist page to upload a copy you are allowed to use, with its credit.
libx.musicbrainz_note: Album covers, album and artist genres, and exact artist matches (better photos and bios), from MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive. Sends artist and album names. MusicBrainz needs no account, but asks apps to say who to contact if something goes wrong; it's sent with each request.
libx.looking_now: Looking up artists... New pictures show up when it's done.
libx.identify_note: Needs an AcoustID key and the MusicBrainz contact above. Song fingerprints (not the audio) go to AcoustID. It only runs when you start it, below.

libx.spotify_how_2: (Spotify asks for one, DJINN doesn't use it); tick Web API; save. Then open the app's Settings, copy the Client ID, choose View client secret and copy that. Saving checks them with Spotify.

With one, it sends only the key and the playlist's id when someone imports a link, nothing about who's asking. YouTube still sees this server's internet address.

lyrp.recheck_note: Recheck reads every song again (for .lrc files added since) and asks LRCLIB again. Export downloads a zip of .lrc files laid out like your music folders and named like the songs, so unzipping it over a music folder puts each one beside its song.
lyrp.import_note: A zip of .lrc or .txt files laid out like your music folders (the same layout as the export above). Each file is matched to a song by the artist and title in its [ar:] and [ti:] lines, or by its place in the zip when those are missing. It only fills songs that have no lyrics: lyrics from song files, tags and LRCLIB always win. Files that look like code or markup are thrown out and listed. Up to 250 MB and 150,000 files per zip; send several zips for a bigger library.

lyrp.better_note: "Better" means timed over plain, or a person's words timed by an AI over plain words. Lyrics an AI made by listening never replace anyone's, and nothing replaces a person's timed lyrics with equal or worse ones.

gg.title: Genre Containers
gg.intro: Group similar genres into containers, so "black metal", "death metal" and "speed metal" all show as "Metal". While this is on, genre lists, the genre cloud and genre pages show the containers instead of the genres in them, and a container's page has every song of its genres. Artist, album and song pages still show the real genres, with the container first in pink. Your music files and the genres DJINN knows aren't changed; turn this off to put everything back.

gg.how: Genres are grouped by DJINN's genre family tree (Admin > Genres > Map). All the way left, each family is one container (Rock, Metal, Electronic...); each step right splits the container with the most songs into its branches, so Rock becomes Hard rock, Punk rock, Alternative rock and so on. Genres the tree doesn't know stay loose. Genres you placed by hand and containers you made or changed are left as they are.

xf.note: Songs from the same album always join without a gap, so live albums and DJ mixes flow as recorded.
rg.off_note: Songs play as loud as they were made.

rg.album_note: Quiet and loud songs on an album keep their difference. Good for playing whole albums.
rg.title: Volume Leveling (ReplayGain)
rg.intro: Keeps songs at an even loudness, so a quiet old track isn't followed by a blast. Uses ReplayGain tags when a file has them. For files without, DJINN measures each song once and keeps the result in its own database; your files aren't changed. Applies from the next song.
rg.boost_note: Leveled songs play quieter than most modern masters. Raise this if everything sounds too soft; songs never get pushed into clipping.
rg.analysis_off: Songs without ReplayGain tags are measured by sound analysis, which is off, so they play unchanged. Switch it on under

eq.party_note: Shape the party mix on every output, including casting and Tune In. Normal levels stay intact; peaks near clipping are softened.

out.intro: Play through more than one device at once, like the stereo and a Bluetooth speaker in the next room. DJINN keeps them in time. Bluetooth lags a few hundred milliseconds behind wired outputs, so raise the delay on the wired ones until everything lines up.

cast.intro: Play the party on Chromecasts, Google TVs, Nest speakers, smart TVs (DLNA), and Sonos, several at once. "Show on TV" puts the TV page on the screen, with what's playing, what's next, and the join code, and plays the music too. Network devices run a few seconds behind this computer's speakers and can't be synced to them, so use either casts or local speakers in a room, not both. Speaker groups from the Google Home app stay in sync with each other.

sp.title: Smart Play
sp.intro: When nobody has requested anything, DJINN picks songs itself. Smart Play has it learn from the party: songs people request come up more, and so do others by the same artists and in the same genres. Songs people skip come up less.
sp.learn: Learn from the party for wild play and radio
sp.playlists: Also use it for shuffled playlists (every song still plays once before any repeats)
sp.mood_note: Everyone at the party gets a dial on the Playing tab, from chill to hype. The auto mix then favors songs whose energy fits what the room wants: faster, punchier songs for hype, calmer ones for chill. Each person's setting counts for 40 minutes. It works for wild play, radio and shuffled playlists, using sound analysis (Admin > Library > Online Info), so songs not analyzed yet aren't moved either way.
sp.styles_note: Each style keeps its own memory, so a Halloween party doesn't change what plays at the family BBQ. Use the one that fits tonight: requests, songs played through, and skips count toward it.
sp.nothing: Nothing yet. It learns as people request and skip songs while this style is in use.

prob.missing_folder_hint: The folder isn't there right now. Plug the drive in or reconnect the share, or remove the folder above if it moved. Its songs stay in DJINN until it's back.
prob.unreadable: Folders and files DJINN can't open
prob.unreadable_hint: DJINN wasn't allowed to read these. Check that the account DJINN runs as can open them, and that network shares are connected.
prob.bad_name_hint: These names use characters that are not valid text, often from an old computer or a ripped CD. Rename the file or folder, then check again.
prob.unsupported_hint: DJINN plays MP3, FLAC, AAC and M4A, Ogg Vorbis and WAV. Convert these to FLAC (full quality) or MP3 with a converter, then check again.
prob.tags_hint: DJINN couldn't read these files' tags, so they show under their file names. Fix the tags with a tag editor such as Mp3tag or MusicBrainz Picard, or use Edit tags on the song, which keeps your changes in DJINN without touching the file.
prob.wont_play_hint: These failed when played or checked, so the file is probably damaged or incomplete. Replace it with a good copy. DJINN tries again when the file changes.
prob.reported_hint: Listeners said these need fixing. Fix the song (Edit tags, a better copy, or a cover in its folder), then select Done to clear the reports.
prob.reported_lyrics_hint: Listeners said these lyrics are wrong or bad. Remove and block takes them away and remembers where they came from, so that source is not used again for the song unless its text changes. Done clears the reports and keeps the lyrics.
prob.duplicate_albums_hint: These albums by one artist hold almost the same songs: a copy in another folder, or the same album under a slightly different name. Keep the better one and remove the other from your music folders, then check for changes. A deluxe edition with extra songs isn't listed, and neither is a song that sits on several albums.
prob.identical_files: The same file twice in one album
prob.identical_files_hint: These songs in one album have the same size, length and title, so they are almost certainly the same file copied. Keep one and remove the other from your music folders, then check for changes.
prob.bogus_values_hint: A track or disc number of 0 or less, or a length of 0, usually means a bad rip or a damaged tag. Fix it with Edit tags or a tag editor. For an MP3 with a length of 0, see the note under "Very short or very long songs".
prob.odd_length: Very short or very long songs
prob.odd_length_hint: Under 10 seconds or over 3 hours. Often a cut-off download, a hidden track, a skit, or a whole mix filed as one song. A variable bit rate MP3 with no length header can also show a wrong length in other players, even though DJINN counts it right. To fix the file: select Fix in the editor, allow the folder under the folders DJINN may change (Admin > Library > Library Editor), unlock the protected area, pick the MP3s, and choose Fix MP3 lengths. It adds the header and can be undone from the editor's history.
prob.low_bitrate_hint: Under 96 kbps, which sounds poor. If you have a better copy, replace the file.
prob.title_junk_hint: A track number in front, "(Official Video)", a web address, spaces around, or all capitals. Clean it with Edit tags, which keeps your change in DJINN, or in a tag editor.
prob.name_mismatch: File names that don't match the title
prob.name_mismatch_hint: The file's name (and folders) don't contain the song's title. Sometimes the tag is right and the name is just different (accents and punctuation count), sometimes the file is mislabeled. Play it to check.
prob.artist_variants_hint: Names that differ only by capitals, a leading "The", "&" or punctuation, so one artist shows twice ("The Beatles" and "Beatles", "AC/DC" and "ACDC"). Pick one spelling and fix the other with Edit tags.
prob.split_across_artists_hint: These albums share a folder and a title but were filed under different artist names, often because of a compilation tag or a "feat." in the album artist. Set the same album artist on all of its songs with Edit album.
prob.cover_differs_hint: The songs of these albums carry more than one cover picture. Embed the same cover in every song, or put one cover.jpg in the folder.
prob.track_gaps: Albums with missing or repeated track numbers
prob.track_gaps_hint: Track numbers that start at 1 with a hole in them (songs missing from the album), or one number used twice. Check that all songs are there and numbered right.
prob.no_lyrics_hint: No lyrics were found in a .lrc file, the tags, an import or LRCLIB. Turn on LRCLIB lookups or import a zip in Library > Lyrics. Instrumentals are fine.
prob.no_loudness_hint: No ReplayGain tags and no measurement, in a library where other songs have them. Turn on ReplayGain in Audio so DJINN measures them.
prob.ai_lyrics_hint: An AI worked on these lyrics. "Words made by an AI" are guesses from listening and may have mistakes: any other source replaces them (LRCLIB is still asked about these songs, and an import of ordinary lyrics replaces them). "Timed by an AI" are a person's words with timing worked out by an AI; the match says how well they fit, so check the low ones. Each row says which import it came from. Use Report these lyrics, then Remove and block, on one that is wrong.
prob.messy_genres_hint: Genre tags that are not one clean genre: several run together with ";" or "|" ("rock;alternative pop rock"), an old genre number like "(17)", a placeholder like "Unknown" or "Other", or a whole sentence. Each one shows as a genre of its own in genre lists, the genre cloud and genre containers. To fix them: select Fix in the editor, pick the songs, choose Genre in the tools under the grid, type the genres with commas between them ("Rock, Alternative") and select Set, then Approve. Editing the Database keeps the change in DJINN only; editing the Library writes it into the files (the folder must be allowed under the folders DJINN may change).
prob.no_length_header_hint: These variable bit rate MP3s have no length header, so many players, phones and car stereos show the wrong length and can't skip ahead properly. DJINN counts them right. To fix the files: select Fix in the editor, allow the folder under the folders DJINN may change (Admin > Library > Library Editor), unlock the protected area, pick the MP3s, and choose Fix MP3 lengths. It adds the header without touching the audio and can be undone from the editor's history. The thorough check reads the start of every MP3 in the background, and again whenever one changes.
prob.vanished_hint: These were in the library and their files are gone (in the last 30 days). If that is a mistake, plug the drive back in or restore the files, then check for changes.
prob.no_artist_hint: Add the artist with Edit tags on the song, or in a tag editor.
prob.no_album_hint: These show as loose songs. Add the album with Edit tags on the song, or in a tag editor.
prob.album_no_cover_hint: Put a cover.jpg in the album's folder or embed a cover with a tag editor. With MusicBrainz on (Library extras, below), DJINN looks covers up.
prob.album_no_year_hint: Add the year with Edit album, or turn on MusicBrainz or Identify songs to fill years in.
prob.album_no_genre_hint: Add a genre with Edit album, or turn on MusicBrainz or AI listening to fill genres in.
